evidence_lineage.claim: The Yardstick Agency is an active, long-established company; financial, pipeline and client-concentration data are unavailable.
Yardstick's public service range spans websites, recurring membership content, a new-firm offer, modular services and strategy work.
Yardstick reports growth to 49 specialists and publishes selected, non-representative client outcome examples.
Yardstick's membership product is an existing recurring content capability with unknown retention performance.
Yardstick has an active public authority content and press presence with unmeasured conversion impact.
The advice sector is consolidating: firm numbers down 15% since 2021 while adviser numbers are stable.
FCA data identifies succession, capacity, digital capability and Consumer Duty as current sector pressures.
Established multi-adviser firms at a change point are proposed as Yardstick's priority audience, unverified against first-party data.
A diagnostic-led service sequence is proposed as a mechanism to improve qualification and retention, not a measured result.

argument_moves.argument: Yardstick has real depth across specialist team size, service range, recurring content and public authority material, but presents these largely as a menu for the whole advice profession rather than tied to a specific business decision a firm is facing.
argument_moves.commercial_consequence: Firms must self-diagnose which service matters to them, which likely slows qualification and risks single-service purchases instead of sequenced, higher-value engagements.
argument_moves.founder_decision: Check whether existing deal records show a pattern of single-service versus multi-service purchases before deciding this is a real constraint.
argument_moves.headline: Yardstick's breadth earns credibility but not a buying decision

argument_moves.argument: FCA data shows firm numbers falling while adviser numbers hold steady, alongside succession, capacity, digital and Consumer Duty pressures — evidence of firms reorganising their business model rather than simply growing it.
argument_moves.commercial_consequence: Positioning at these change points rather than as a general supplier could allow earlier qualification and routing to larger service combinations, though no pipeline evidence yet confirms higher conversion or spend.
argument_moves.founder_decision: Decide whether to name specific change points in the public offer or continue competing on service breadth alone.
argument_moves.headline: Sector consolidation creates defined change points Yardstick could own

argument_moves.argument: The growth logic depends on four connected levers: change-moment qualified demand, diagnostic-to-project conversion, service sequence value and retained proof and referral. Each draws on an existing Yardstick asset, but none has a measured baseline.
argument_moves.commercial_consequence: Treating this as a cosmetic repositioning rather than four measurable levers risks a change with no way to judge whether it worked.
argument_moves.founder_decision: Commission baseline measurement on at least one lever, such as current diagnostic-to-project conversion, before committing budget to repositioning.
argument_moves.headline: Four linked levers drive the opportunity, not one message change

argument_moves.argument: Given FCA sector data and Yardstick's project-level service depth, established multi-adviser firms facing succession, acquisition, recruitment or client-selection decisions are the most plausible priority audience; newer or very small firms are already served by the existing Made Simple offer.
argument_moves.commercial_consequence: Prioritising this audience publicly could raise deal size and attach if the hypothesis holds, but could also narrow apparent relevance to smaller firms currently served well.
argument_moves.founder_decision: Test this audience priority against actual client and pipeline records before any public repositioning.
argument_moves.headline: Established multi-adviser firms at a change point are the best-fit hypothesis, not a confirmed segment

argument_moves.argument: Reorganise the public offer around named firm change points with a diagnostic as the main entry mechanism, sequencing strategy, website, project and recurring content according to diagnosed need, using capability Yardstick already has.
argument_moves.commercial_consequence: Without pipeline and segmentation evidence this remains a mechanism for improving qualification and sequencing, not a sized revenue outcome; any scenario is illustrative only.
argument_moves.founder_decision: Approve a bounded pilot — one change-point narrative, one diagnostic flow — with defined measurement, before deciding on a full proposition rewrite.
argument_moves.headline: Lead with a change-point diagnostic, validate before wider rollout

audience_opportunity.commercial_moment: FCA data shows consolidation (firm count down 15% since 2021 while adviser numbers hold) plus sector-wide pressure from succession, capacity, digital capability and Consumer Duty, indicating many firms are actively reconsidering their commercial model.
audience_opportunity.commercial_relevance: These are moments when marketing investment decisions are made at business-model level rather than routine brand upkeep, which fits Yardstick's project and strategy services better than its lighter Made Simple offer for new firms.
audience_opportunity.priority_audience: Established multi-adviser firms facing a change point such as succession, acquisition, recruitment or deliberate client-selection strategy (hypothesis, unverified against Yardstick's own client base).
audience_opportunity.validation_required: Yardstick pipeline, win-loss records and client segmentation showing which firm types actually convert into higher-value engagements.

business_opportunity.commercial_consequence: If qualification and sequencing improve, deal size and service attach could grow; no baseline conversion, pricing or contribution data exists to size this.
business_opportunity.growth_mechanism: A diagnostic entry point maps a firm's change point to a defined sequence of strategy, website, project and recurring content services, rather than presenting services as a flat menu.
business_opportunity.statement: Yardstick's broad service portfolio and authority content are not currently organised around the specific commercial decisions that push an advice firm to buy more substantial marketing help.
business_opportunity.validation_required: Yardstick's actual deal mix, conversion rates by service and current attach rates between first purchase and follow-on project work.

founder_argument.central_argument: Yardstick has rare category depth, a 49-person specialist team, recurring content, project services and a large public authority footprint, but its public offer still reads as a menu for the whole advice profession. FCA data shows a consolidating sector (firm count down 15% since 2021, adviser numbers stable) where firms face succession, capacity, digital and client-selection decisions. The commercial opportunity is to reorganise Yardstick's existing capability around these named change points, using a diagnostic to route firms into the right service sequence and recurring content as retained proof. This is a hypothesis requiring pipeline validation, not a confirmed segment or forecast.

commercial_growth_mechanism.growth_equation: Change-moment qualified demand x diagnostic-to-project conversion x service sequence value x retained proof and referral = more valuable, longer-lived client relationships
known_inputs: Broad existing service portfolio across strategy, website, project and recurring content (Y2)
Recurring membership content capability already in market (Y4)
Established authority content and press footprint (Y5)
Sector consolidation and change-point pressures from FCA data (Y6, Y7)
missing_inputs: Yardstick pipeline volume and source mix (Y1)
Conversion rate from first contact to diagnostic to project (Y8, Y9)
Service attach and sequencing rates across existing clients (Y9)
Segment-level revenue, margin and client concentration (Y1)
Retention and referral rates from membership and project clients (Y4)

evidence_basis.claim: The Yardstick Agency is an active, long-established company with a named founder, but financial and pipeline data are not publicly available.
Yardstick offers a broad portfolio spanning bespoke websites, recurring content membership, a new-firm offer, modular services and marketing strategy.
Yardstick has grown to 49 specialists and publishes selected client outcome examples that cannot establish typical performance.
Yardstick's membership service is an existing recurring content and distribution capability with unknown retention and attach rates.
Yardstick maintains a substantial public authority footprint through guides, checklists and press coverage, with unknown conversion into qualified demand.
The UK advice sector is consolidating, with firm numbers down 15% since 2021 while adviser numbers remain broadly stable.
FCA data identifies succession, capacity, digital capability and Consumer Duty as material pressures facing advice firms.
Established multi-adviser firms at a change point are the most plausible priority audience for Yardstick, but this is unverified against any Yardstick client or pipeline data.
A diagnostic-led offer connecting a firm's change point to a sequenced set of Yardstick services could improve qualification and retention, but this is a proposed mechanism, not a measured outcome.

strategic_recommendation.competitor_substitution_test: A generic 'marketing agency for advisers' claim could be made by any competitor; this argument instead ties Yardstick's specific combination of specialist team scale, recurring proof content and project depth to named sector change points evidenced by FCA data, which is harder to substitute without equivalent breadth and evidence.
strategic_recommendation.next_decision: Commission a pipeline and segmentation review of existing Yardstick clients to test whether change-point firms convert and spend more, before committing to a full proposition rewrite.
strategic_recommendation.recommendation: Reorganise the public offer around named firm change points, with a diagnostic as the primary entry mechanism, before investing in any broader messaging or campaign activity.
strategic_recommendation.tradeoffs: A change-point narrative may read as less relevant to newer or smaller firms currently served by the Made Simple offer, so Yardstick must decide whether to run both propositions in parallel or fully reposition.
strategic_recommendation.why_this: Yardstick already owns the required assets (specialist breadth, membership content, project services, authority content); the gap is how they are organised and presented, not new capability.
